question_text: According to the course material, co-operation in Nigeria started as far back as 1907; notable among the earliest co-operative societies was Agege Planters Union (A.P.U), made up of cocoa producers numbering about:
explanation: APU was made up of about 400 cocoa farmers.

question_text: According to the course material, reasons cocoa farmers joined together included pooling resources to purchase inputs at reduced prices, exchanging ideas on how to produce the best quality cocoa, and collectively fighting for:
explanation: They pooled resources, exchanged ideas, and fought for government recognition.

question_text: According to the course material, colonial cooperative legislation in 1935 was based on the report of Mr. F.F. Strickland; with another Strickland report submitted in 1936, Co-operative Thrift and Credit Societies (C.T.C.S) were formed and spread all over:
explanation: The 1936 Strickland report led to CTCS across Eastern and Western Nigeria.

question_text: According to the course material, the initial achievement of government on Co-operatives was the promulgation of Co-operative Laws and the Co-operative Regulations which followed on:
explanation: Co-operative Laws and Regulations followed on 6 February 1936.

question_text: According to the course material, in 1937 Gbedun Co-operative Produce Marketing Society became the first Co-operative Society to be the first Registrar of Co-operative Societies in:
explanation: Gbedun became the first registered co-operative society in Nigeria in 1937.

question_text: According to the course material, in 1953 The Co-operative bank Plc was established; a sum of One Million Pounds (part of cocoa export proceeds) was approved for take-off by the late Chief Obafemi Awolowo, then Premier of the:
explanation: Awolowo, Premier of the Western Region, approved one million pounds for the bank.

question_text: According to the course material, the Co-operative Federation of Nigeria was formed in 1945 and formally registered in:
explanation: CFN was formed in 1945 and formally registered in 1967.

question_text: According to the course material, factors responsible for failure of cooperatives movement in Nigeria include inappropriate government political stability, poor cooperative education, dishonesty of cooperative leaders, disloyalty of membership, inadequate supervision, mismanagement of fund, lack of infrastructure, lack of finance, poor leadership, pseudo/disguised cooperative, poor management, policy inconsistency, and:
explanation: The material lists 13 constraints including poor record keeping and account.

question_text: According to the course material, traditional savings and lending patterns common in Nigeria include ESUSU in Yorubaland and ADASHI in:
explanation: ESUSU in Yorubaland and ADASHI in Ibo land are cited as traditional cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, the main tenet of modern acts of cooperative is:
explanation: Voluntarism is the main tenet of modern cooperative acts.

question_text: According to the course material, there are definite rules and regulations governing co-operatives as spelt in the co-operatives Decree of:
explanation: Co-operatives are governed by the Co-operatives Decree of 1993 plus state laws and by-laws.

question_text: According to the course material, a co-operative is a long-term concern that outlives its founding fathers, so sustainability in co-operative is higher than that of self-help organization, some of which operate on:
explanation: Self-help organisations may operate on an ad-hoc basis unlike long-term cooperatives.

question_text: According to the course material, areas of similarities between co-operative and self-help organisation include identical interests or goals, roles, shared values, communication, and members may enjoy a:
explanation: Similarities include identical interests, roles, values, communication and common identity.

question_text: According to the course material, the organizational structure of cooperation is a four-tier system with the mother union at the apex and primary societies at the base (Oshuntogun 1971); it consists of primary, secondary, tertiary and:
explanation: The four tiers are primary, secondary, tertiary and apex.

question_text: According to the course material, members of Primary Societies are individuals (natural persons); examples include Cooperative Consumer Society (CCS) and:
explanation: Primary examples include CCS and CTCS.

question_text: According to the course material, members of Secondary Cooperative Societies are corporate bodies or primary cooperative societies; examples are Cooperative Produce and Marketing Union (CPMU) and:
explanation: Secondary examples include CPMU and CTCU.

question_text: According to the course material, the tertiary is known as league of unions which operates at the state level; examples include League of Cooperative Thrift and Credit Union (LCTUC) and:
explanation: Tertiary examples include LCTUC and LCFU.

question_text: According to the course material, examples of national apex organizations are the Cooperative Federation of Nigeria (CFN) and National Association of Cooperative Credit Union of Nigeria (NACCUN); regional apex examples are Cooperative Supply Association (CSA) and:
explanation: ANCE and CSA are regional apex organisations.

question_text: According to the course material, at the international level co-operatives are united under one umbrella of the:
explanation: ICA is the international umbrella of co-operatives.

question_text: According to the course material, ANCE comprises several Co-operative Produce Marketing unions in Oyo, Ondo, Ogun, Lagos and Ekiti States; it is established for exporting good quality Cocoa, Coffee and Palm kernels and also specialises in livestock feeds known as:
explanation: ANCE specialises in ANCE FEEDS as well as cocoa, coffee and palm kernels.

question_text: According to the course material, since its inception in 1945 ANCE has received several international awards; its ultra-modern office complex, ANCE BUILDING, is on Magazine Road, Oricho,
explanation: ANCE BUILDING on Magazine Road, Ibadan, is the head office.

question_text: According to the course material, National Association of Co-operative Credit Unions of Nigeria (NACCUN) was formed in 1970 for the propagation and development of Co-operative Credit Societies; its administrative office is situated at plot 5, Adelabu Close, opposite Custom & Excise Training School,
explanation: NACCUN office is at plot 5 Adelabu Close, Ikeja Lagos.

question_text: According to the course material, the Nigerian Agricultural Co-operative Marketing Organisation (NACMO) was established as a national co-operative apex in:
explanation: NACMO was established in 1987.

question_text: According to the course material, CFN is a member of the International Co-operatives Alliance (ICA) as well as the:
explanation: CFN is a member of ICA and IFAP.

question_text: According to the course material, National Cooperative Insurance Society Nigeria Limited (NCIS) was established on November 25th, 1977 and on 9th July 1980 was registered to continue as a conventional insurer under the:
explanation: NCIS was registered 9 July 1980 under the Insurance Decree of 1976.

question_text: According to the course material, the World Council of Credit Unions (WOCCU) is the global trade association and development agency for credit unions, headquartered in Madison, USA; worldwide, 49,000 credit unions in 97 countries serve:
explanation: 49,000 credit unions in 97 countries serve 184 million people.

question_text: According to the course material, WOCCU has created financial tools including its flagship PEARLS monitoring system, a set of financial ratios or indicators that help:
explanation: PEARLS is a set of financial ratios that help standardise terminology among institutions.

question_text: According to the course material, IFAP was established in 1946 as an organization that advocated at the international level for member farm organizations; it was liquidated by the French Tribunal de Grande Instance in a judgment made on:
explanation: IFAP was liquidated on 4 November 2010 after an economic and political crisis.

question_text: According to the course material, International Fund for Agricultural Development (IFAD) was established in 1977 by a United Nations specialized Agency as an international financial institution from the outcome of the:
explanation: IFAD was established in 1977 from the 1974 World Food Conference.

question_text: According to the course material, IFAD mission is to enable poor rural people to overcome poverty; it focuses on country-specific solutions which can involve increasing poor people's access to financial services, market, technology, land and other:
explanation: IFAD focuses on access to finance, markets, technology, land and other natural resources.

question_text: According to the course material, the International Co-operative Alliance was founded in 1895; currently ICA has 267 member organisations from 97 countries, representing approximately:
explanation: ICA has 267 member organisations from 97 countries representing about 1 billion individuals.

question_text: According to the course material, according to the I.C.A. monthly journal, the International Co-operative Alliance in continuation of the work of the Rochdale Equitable Pioneers seeks to promote a non-profit system of production and trade organized in the interests of the whole community and based upon:
explanation: ICA seeks a non-profit system based upon voluntary and mutual self-help.

question_text: According to the course material, ICA's most significant publication is the Review of International Co-operation, a monthly journal published in English, French and:
explanation: The Review of International Co-operation is published in English, French and German.

question_text: According to the course material, the International Co-operative Alliance's office is at 15, Route de Morillons, 1218 Grand-Saconnex,
explanation: ICA office is at 15 Route de Morillons, 1218 Grand-Saconnex, Geneva, Switzerland.

question_text: According to the course material, Umebali (2008) observed prospects for cooperatives in Nigeria including universities awarding degrees in co-operatives such as Enugu State University of Science and Technology, Nnamdi Azikiwe University, Olabisi Onabanjo University and:
explanation: NOUN is listed among universities awarding degrees in co-operatives.
